name: Spork
notes: The second shader, from Spork's own project file (`Big Samson.blend`), with his permission and on the terms he gave the user: his shader ships complete, including the third-party parts, as long as the credits stay in place. Built by `build_spork_library.py` in `UmaViewer-DevTools`, which appends his `Simple Diff + Shaded` group and four materials into `SporkShaders.blend` and unbinds every image (a library carries slots, not textures - the apply step loads them from the model's folder). Measured in `docs/SHADER_INTERFACE.md` section 6 and re-measured with `shader_manifest_names.py`: the group is 26 nodes, has no subgroups and no image nodes, and offers exactly four sockets - `Diffuse` (colour, default 0.5 grey), `Shaded` (colour, default black), `Shadow Softness` (float, 0.15), `Emission Strength` (float, 0.0). It is a genuinely different mechanism from Looper's: a `Diffuse BSDF` into `Shader to RGB` shaped by `Shadow Softness` through a `Map Range`, mixed with a flat `Shaded` colour - the same idea as 0.2.6's world-light option done smoothly, which is what our own reverted patch borrowed from him (`docs/WORLD_LIGHT_INFLUENCE.md` section 6). **Only two of his four sockets are settings**: `Diffuse` and `Shaded` are *fed by the material's own textures* in every one of his materials (measured: `mmd_base_tex.Color -> Group.Diffuse`, `Image Texture.001.Color -> Group.Shaded` in all six of his wrappers), so a panel row for them would drive a socket whose link overrides it - a control that cannot do anything, which 2.23.2 removed on purpose. `Shadow Softness` and `Emission Strength` are the two he set by hand, and they are the two rows below. Material roles: his template wrapper (`mtl_chr1101_00_hair`, the one with all four texture slots) is renamed `Spork Shader` and is what `parts` map onto; `Spork Eye` is his eyeball material and `Spork Eye Inner` his lit inner eye. His eyes are the one place his file needs somebody else's node: `Spork Eye` reads its UVs through mmd_tools' own `MMDTexUV` group (5 nodes), which travels with the material and is not an unknown dependency - mmd_tools is required by this add-on anyway. Nothing else third-party comes with this library: `SarlShader1.003` (73 nodes) and `Enhancer-Skin.002` (13) are used by exactly one of his materials, `See Thru`, which matches none of this manifest's part substrings, and the eight `.FONDANT_Normals_2.1.0_4.5_*` groups are in his file but no material of his reaches them (measured). His file's only credit text is a note for a different model (Lumine), so the credits for this shader are the ones in this note and in `docs/SPORK_RIG.md`. The outline is ours, both halves: `outline.blend` names `Umashaders.blend`, so the shell's group *and* its material come out of that file (2.24.0 did the group, 2.26.0 the material), and `Uma Outline Material` is also in this library's collection so that a manifest resolving it locally would still find ours. **One caveat to read before asking a question about eyes**: a plain UmaViewer export names exactly one eye material (`mtl_chr1001_00_eye` in the reference model), so `eye_inner` - matched on `eye inner`/`eye_inner` - fires only for a model that has such a material. His own project does; the exports this add-on is for may not.

settings.description: How far the lit side fades into the shaded side. His own default is 0.15; 0 is a hard two-tone split and 1 is the whole band
Glow added on top of the shaded look, off at 0.0 as his own files ship it
